recipes.name: Jalapeno Snacks
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 ounce) package dry ranch salad dressing mix
20 large jalapeno peppers, halved and seeded
1 pound sliced bacon, cut in half

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Stir together the cream cheese, Cheddar cheese, mayonnaise, ranch dressing mix, and garlic powder in a mixing bowl until evenly blended. Spoon some of the cheese mixture into each jalapeno half, wrap with half a bacon strip, and secure with a toothpick. Arrange the wrapped jalapeno halves onto a broiler pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until the bacon is no longer pink and beginning to brown, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Jalapeno Snacks
raw_recipe.description: These bacon-wrapped, cream cheese-stuffed jalapenos are addictive.

review.reviewBody: try to boil the bacon before you start. it is still close to the texture of uncooked bacon, and you can still wrap it around the pepper, and use the toothpick to hold it, but you cook off the fat, so your bacon gets crunchy in the oven instead of greasy

Thanks Mrs. Houston. Delicious as written, husband loved it, but I like things a little less salty. The second time I made these I subbed in light cream cheese, ranch dressing for the ranch mix and mayo, fresh grated sharp cheddar and added a couple of dashes of tabasco. As other people have said, use gloves when working with the jalapeños.Let the bacon get to room temperature so it wraps easily (sometimes I use a whole piece of bacon for each one - mmmmm, then no need for a toothpick!) I put the cream cheese ingredients etc. for the filling in a quart size ziplock, smoosh together, then snip off an end to fill the jalapeños. Use the broiler pan as directed so the fat drips away from the poppers and they get crispy. In my oven they took about 30 minutes. These are now in regular rotation for football games and holidays.

This was the best recipe I have tried on this site for jalapeno poppers not fried. I basically followed the recipe with just a few changes.
1. I have a jalapeno rack so I left them whole & cored them out, leaving a few seeds for heat.
2. I used mozzarella cheese instead of cheddar because I didn't have any.
3. To make the mixture thin enough to pipe into the jalapenos, I thinned the mixture out with a couple TBSP of milk.
4. I put the mixture in a plastic baggy and cut the tip off to pipe it into the jalapenos.
5. Then I topped each one with approximately a 1/4 piece of bacon folded up and placed on top.
6. Cooked according to directions.

Yummy! Didn't have ranch seasoning so omitted the mayo and just put 1/4 cup of ranch dressing. Precooked bacon in skillet about halfway and blotted on paper towels. Baked on cookie cooling rack inside shallow lip pan. Did remove all veins and seeds with melon baller, but luckily didn't have time to soak in cold water and they were not too hot at all. Only took about 15 minutes precooking bacon. We will definitely be making these again. I think the ranch flavoring is what others I have tried have been missing.

I used skewers to hold the bacon in place. I then put them on a broiler pan and put them in the smoker. This lets the grease drip off and leaves all the flavor! I smoked them for 30 minutes at 180 degrees and then 30 minutes at 350 degrees. They were heavenly!!!

Very tasty. I soaked halved and seeded jalapenos in ice water for 2 hours to mellow out the heat a bit. I substituted sour cream for mayo and used turkey bacon bits for a healthier, less greasy, treat. I also added two tablespoons of chopped cilantro. Delicious!

I have made this recipe more times than I would like to admit and have discovered how to get great finishes on it by using these tips: To get the bacon crispy: Buy thin bacon, or use a rolling pin and flatten out thick bacon. Mild cheddar cheese seems to get the best results. Also, if you do not have dry ranch salad dressing, you can make your own by using about a tablespoon (more or less, just equal amount of both) each of garlic and onion powder. I tend to taste it after stirring to make it just right. Lastly, after mixing all the ingredients, I let them infuse for about 20 to 30 minutes before stuffing the peppers.

I don't think people understand just how good this recipe is. Whenever I take it somewhere new, I tell people that I'm making jalapeno poppers and they always tell me about a recipe they do. All I can do is smile at them while in my head I think, "they've never had THESE before!" It never fails...when I bring them for people to have, they all say they are the best they've ever had. I have even had more than one person say it is the best thing they've ever eaten!

Like somebody else said, soak the cut and seeded peppers in ice water for 45 minutes and it takes out the heat but leaves all the flavor. Also, instead of wrapping the bacon around the jalapeno, I just lay a slice right on top lengthwise. That cooks the bacon more evenly. The other thing I do is to cook these on a smoker. I put a wire rack down with a layer of foil underneath it to keep the bottom from burning. It's way better than in the oven.

These are so good I made an account just so I could review them. Try it and you'll know what all the fuss is about.

As written, this recipe is just too greasy for my tastes. The filling was awesome and the peppers were perfect but the bacon was not good. It was under cooked and made everything a greasy mess. I made a few with just bacon bits on top and they turned out perfect. Next time I make these I will use about half the amount of bacon, cook it first and crumble it on top before baking to cut down on the grease.

Absolutely the best jalapeño poppers out there! I make them for every get together, they never last long and I am always asked for the recipe. I do bake them at 425 because it gets the bacon actually cooked through so it’s not rubbery. One 8 Oz cream cheese package never seems to be enough for that many poppers so I basically double the recipe, but don’t use two full ranch packets. I place one toothpick in each end of the bacon and ensure it goes all the way through the other side, otherwise it doesn’t hold well (I use thick cut bacon and slice in half). Perfect recipe!

We made this for a tailgate and loved it - with two changes that we made. Instead of wrapping it in bacon, we cooked the bacon ahead of time, chopped it up and added it to the mixture that we stuffed the jalapeno's with. We also added a small slice of pepperjack cheese on top of each stuffed jalapeno as we grilled them. Delish!
Since I do not eat bacon, I will omit it. Instead I can wrap with a strip of hard tofu!

I make this recipe as is and love it. Many people complain how greasy the bacon makes it. I put a wire baking/cooling rack on an aluminum foil line baking sheet to bake them and they turn out perfect. The aluminum foil also helps with clean up. I originally printed this recipe off in 2010 and have been making it ever since. One of my most requested appetizers to bring to gatherings!
We love these! I now leave the stem on when halving so cream cheese doesn’t leak out. I also added a little onion powder for some flavor.
These were great! I made these following directions, except I followed suggestion to boil the bacon before wrapping the jalapenos. They turned out so good!

All I can say is OH MY GOSH!! These are AMAZING! I soaked my jalapenos in ice water for about 4 hours after deseeding them (which I would say reduced them to medium heat)and used bacon crumbled on top as another suggested, but otherwise followed the directions exactly. Other than a tiny bit salty, they are definitely 5 stars!

SO DELICIOUS! Will definitely make again. DON'T use thick cut bacon though. I had to cook about 35 minutes for the bacon to get done. DO wrap your bacon all the way around the pepper and push your toothpick all the way through the pepper. I made a half recipe (just two of us) because it makes so much. If I made this for a party I would make the whole recipe and prep them ahead of time and refrigerate then pop into oven when the guests arrive. I'm sure they would be a hit with my friends.
This was easy and delicious. Love the cheese mixture
Boiling the bacon first was an excellent idea. They turned out great. I used smaller homegrown jalapeños and had plenty of cheese left. I would do this recipe again in a heartbeat.
Very easy to make. Bought 20 jalapeños and had to double up on the filling to fill the 40 halves.
